title: Sell Mineral Rights in Marianna, PA
metaTitle: Sell Mineral Rights in Marianna, PA
metaDescription: Marianna, Washington County carries the legacy of a historic coal mining disaster alongside modern Marcellus wet-gas rights. What that means for owners.
heroLead: Marianna is a small Washington County borough forever tied to the 1908 mine disaster that struck this community, and its mineral title today still reflects that deep coal-mining history.
intro: The Marianna mine explosion of December 1908 was one of the deadliest disasters in Pennsylvania coal history, and it happened at an operation that, like most coal companies of that era, held mineral rights across a wide swath of the surrounding land. A century and change later, the coal is largely mined out or left in place for safety reasons, but the old severed mineral estates from that era are still very much a factor in how gas rights are sorted out around Marianna today.

sections.heading: Coal-Era Severances Complicate Gas Title
paragraphs: Because coal companies here often acquired broad mineral reservations that predate the modern gas industry entirely, tracing who currently owns the oil and gas rights on a Marianna-area parcel means working through a corporate succession that can span more than a hundred years and several different company names.

The scale of the Marianna disaster meant significant public and legal attention at the time, which in some cases left an unusually well-documented paper trail for researchers like us tracing mineral ownership more than a century later.

sections.heading: Washington County's Core Wet-Gas Position
paragraphs: Whatever the coal history, Marianna sits inside Washington County's core Marcellus wet-gas window, among the most heavily leased and drilled territory anywhere in the play. That activity level means real value can exist even on parcels with a complicated coal-era title history.

sections.heading: What We Trace Before Making an Offer
paragraphs: We follow the corporate chain from the original coal-era mineral reservation to whoever currently holds it, confirm whether oil and gas were included in that reservation or left separate, and check current unit and lease activity before discussing value.

faqs.question: Does the old coal company still technically own our gas rights?
faqs.answer: Possibly, through a corporate successor — we trace that chain specifically rather than assuming it lapsed or transferred automatically.

faqs.question: Were oil and gas typically included in the old Marianna coal reservations?
faqs.answer: It varies by the specific deed language, which is why we read the original document rather than assuming based on the era.

faqs.question: Is this area still an active part of the Marcellus play?
faqs.answer: Washington County remains one of the most heavily developed wet-gas counties in Pennsylvania, and we check current status for the specific Marianna-area parcel.

faqs.question: Is it common for Marianna families to not know their coal-era mineral history?
faqs.answer: Very common — most people we talk to here know about the 1908 disaster but have never seen the actual mineral deed tied to their own property until we pull it.
